readings: Sum results.points for each race name (joining races to results on raceId). Take the average of those per-race-name totals. Keep the race names whose total is above that average. Return one row with three values. First, the combined total points of those race names. Second, the average of results.laps over all individual result rows belonging to those race names. Third, the average of (race-name total minus the average total) across those race names.

Sum results.points for each race name (joining races to results on raceId). Take the average of those per-race-name totals. Keep the race names whose total is above that average. Return one row with three values. First, the combined total points of those race names. Second, the average laps completed computed per race name (the average of results.laps within each race name), then averaged across those race names, so each race name counts equally. Third, the average of (race-name total minus the average total) across those race names.
queries:
WITH name_totals AS (
  SELECT r.name AS name, SUM(res.points) AS total
  FROM races r
  JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
avg_total AS (
  SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_t FROM name_totals
),
kept AS (
  SELECT name, total FROM name_totals, avg_total WHERE total > avg_t
)
SELECT
  (SELECT SUM(total) FROM kept) AS total_points,
  (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL))
   FROM races r
   JOIN results res ON res.raceId = r.raceId
   WHERE r.name IN (SELECT name FROM kept)) AS avg_laps,
  (SELECT AVG(total - avg_t) FROM kept, avg_total) AS avg_diff;
WITH t AS (
  SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS total, AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) AS al
  FROM races r
  JOIN results res ON r.raceId = res.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
), a AS (
  SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t
)
SELECT SUM(t.total), AVG(t.al), AVG(t.total - a.av)
FROM t, a
WHERE t.total > a.av;
